# Introduction

This Quarto document presents the analysis of FTMS LC-MSn flaxseed data for selecting one representative spectral tree per feature. Preprocessing and feature definition was performed in [Preprocessing steps](ftms_preprocessing).

# Data import

Loading all required libraries and importing the results from the data preprocessing.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(xcms)
library(MsExperiment)
library(Spectra)
library(readxl)
library(IRanges)
library(S4Vectors)
library(here)
library(RDynLib)
register(SerialParam())
pth <- getwd()
pth
```

First we load the `XcmsExperiment` ftms object with the preprocessing results.

```{r}
load(file.path(pth, "data", "ftms.RData"))
class(ftms)
```

# Associate MS2 spectra to features

Next, we use `xcms::featureSpectra()` to extract all MS2 spectra for each feature from `ftms` object.

> The `xcms::featureSpectra()` function returns a `Spectra` object.
>
> When using `msLevel = 2`, the resulting `Spectra` object contains all MS2 spectra whose retention time and precursor m/z fall within the ranges of any chromatographic peak of a feature.

```{r}
ms2 <- featureSpectra(dropFilledChromPeaks(ftms), msLevel = 2, skipFilled = TRUE)

msLevel(ms2) |>
  table()
```

it returns `r length(ms2)` MS level 2 spectra. The total number of features for which an MS2 spectrum was identified is:

```{r}
length(unique(ms2$feature_id))
length(ms2$feature_id)
```

Here we print the initial number of MS levels.

```{r}
s <- spectra(ftms)
table(msLevel(s))
```

In total, there were `r table(msLevel(s))[2]` MS2 spectra. This means that `r round((table(msLevel(s))[2]-length(ms2$feature_id))*100/table(msLevel(s))[2], 1)` % of the MS2 spectra could not be assigned to any chromatographic peak.

The percentage of features with at least one MS2:

```{r}
# Total number of features in ftms
n_total_features <- nrow(featureDefinitions(ftms))

# Features with ≥1 MS2 (those returned by featureSpectra)
n_features_with_ms2 <- length(unique(ms2$feature_id))

# Percentage
perc_features_with_ms2 <- (n_features_with_ms2 / n_total_features) * 100
perc_features_with_ms2

```

The total number of features with at least one MS2 is `r n_features_with_ms2`, which corresponds to `r format(perc_features_with_ms2, digits = 3)`%.

A summary on the number of MS2 spectra assigned to a feature is shown below:

```{r}
table(ms2$feature_id) |>
    quantile()
```

The median number of MS2 spectra per feature (across all data files) is hence `r median(table(ms2$feature_id))`.

the percentage of MS2 spectra that are assigned to a feature

```{r}
# Total number of MS2 spectra in the dataset
n_total_ms2 <- sum(msLevel(s) == 2)
sp <- spectraData(ms2)
sp$groups <- paste0(sp$dataOrigin, "_", sp$scanIndex)
# Number of MS2 spectra assigned to features
n_assigned_ms2 <- length(unique(sp$groups))

# Percentage assigned
perc_ms2_assigned <- (n_assigned_ms2 / n_total_ms2) * 100
perc_ms2_assigned

```

The total number of assigned MS2 spectra is `r n_assigned_ms2`, which corresponds to a percentage of `r format(perc_ms2_assigned, digits = 3)`.

Note that an MS2 spectrum could also be assigned to more than one feature. The total number of MS2 spectra assigned to more than one feature is:

```{r}
ms2_id <- paste0(ms2$dataOrigin, "_", ms2$acquisitionNum)
ms2_table <- table(ms2_id)
ms2_mult <- names(ms2_table)[ms2_table > 1]

```

Of the `r length(unique(ms2_id))` MS2 spectra, `r length(ms2_mult)` are assigned to more than one feature.

# Extract all MS2-MSn spectra associated to features

We next extract the full MSn tree for features. The `RDynLib::ftms_all_levels()`function retrieves, from an `XcmsExperiment` object, all MS3 (and subsequently MS4 spectra) that are associated with MS2 spectra in a given `Spectra` object, and returns a combined `Spectra` object containing all MS2, MS3, and MS4 spectra, with each spectrum linked to a feature via a propagated `feature_id` from the originally matched MS2 spectrum.

```{r}
ftms_msn_tree <- ftms_all_levels(ftms,ms2)

table(msLevel(ftms_msn_tree))
```

The number of spectra from different MS levels is shown below:

```{r}
table(msLevel(ftms_msn_tree))
```

# Grouping MSn spectra into spectral trees

We now group all spectra that belong to the same spectral tree and record the precursor m/z of the originating MS2 spectrum for each spectrum within that tree.

The function `RDYnLib::assign_msntree_id()` will:

-   Take a `Spectra` object `x` containing MS2–MSn spectra\

-   Assign tree IDs to each spectrum in `x`, based on precursor relationships within each sample (`dataOrigin`)\

-   Ensure that MS2 spectra always start a new tree, and that MS3/MS4 spectra inherit the tree ID from their parent\

-   Propagate the MS2-level precursor m/z to all downstream spectra in the same tree (MS3, MS4, …), with `NA` for MS2 spectra\

-   Return the updated `Spectra` object with two new spectra variables:

    -   **`MSntreeID`** — integer ID of the fragmentation tree each spectrum belongs to\
    -   **`precursorMz.MS2`** — MS2-level precursor m/z propagated to MS3/MS4 (and beyond), `NA` for MS2

```{r}
ftms_msn_tree <- assign_msntree_id(ftms_msn_tree)
spectraVariables(ftms_msn_tree)
```

```{r}
length(unique(ftms_msn_tree$MSntreeID))
```

There are in total `r length(unique(ftms_msn_tree$MSntreeID))` spectral (fragmentation) trees for in total `r length(unique(ftms_msn_tree$feature_id))` features. The distribution of the lengths of the fragmentation trees is

```{r}
ftms_msn_tree$MSntreeID |>
    table() |>
    quantile()

table(table(ftms_msn_tree$MSntreeID))
```

Fragmentation trees have maximally 4 spectra. This is in accordance with the setup of the ion trap instrument: The two most intense first order product ions were refragmented (if their intensity was above a threshold), resulting in maximally two MS3 spectra, and the most intense second order product ion of the most intense first order product ion was also refragmented (if it's intensity was above a threshold), resulting in maximally one MS4 spectrum. So, a fragmentation tree can maximally consist of one MS2 spectrum + two MS3 spectra + one MS4 spectrum = four spectra.

```{r}
## we stored the tree ids and the msLevels to a dataframe
df <- spectraData(ftms_msn_tree, c("MSntreeID", "msLevel")) |>
    as.data.frame()

## here we take count the last level of each tree
library(dplyr)
max_level_per_tree <- df %>%
  group_by(MSntreeID) %>%
  summarise(max_level = max(msLevel), .groups = "drop")


print(t <- table(max_level_per_tree$max_level))

```

The number of trees that go up to MS2 level is : `r t[1]`. The number of trees that go up to MS3 level is : `r t[2]`. The number of trees that go up to MS4 level is : `r t[3]`.

# Select single best MSn spectral tree per feature

#calling the global functions

```{r}
#source("best_ftms_tree_pipeline.R")

ftms_obj <- ftms_msn_tree

# 1. selection
res <- best_tree_pipeline(ftms_obj)
# the number of trees (it should be equal to the number of unique features)
res$best_trees |> nrow()
```

```{r}
ftms_best <- res$ftms_best
```

Enrichment of the selected trees

```{r}
#source("best_ftms_tree_pipeline.R")
ftms_final <- enrich_ms3_ms4(
  ftms_best = res$ftms_best,
  sd_filtered = res$sd_filtered,
  ftms_msn_tree = ftms_msn_tree
)

# Check enrichment
length(res$ftms_best)
length(ftms_final)

# Check the number of merged trees
length(unique(ftms_final$MergedMSntreeID))

# Compare MS levels
table(Spectra::msLevel(res$ftms_best))
table(Spectra::msLevel(ftms_final))

length(unique(unlist(ftms_final$feature_id)))
length(unique(unlist(ftms_final$MergedMSntreeID)))
length(unique(unlist(ftms_final$MSntreeID)))
```

statistics

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Average number of spectra per feature before and after enrichment
comparison <- data.frame(
  stage = c("Before enrichment", "After enrichment"),
  n_features = c(
    length(unique(ftms_best$feature_id)),
    length(unique(ftms_final$feature_id))
  ),
  n_spectra = c(
    length(ftms_best),
    length(ftms_final)
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    mean_spectra = round(n_spectra / n_features, 2)
  )

print(comparison)
```

Average number of MS2, MS3 and MS4 spectra per feature

```{r}
# Function to calculate averages by MS level
average_ms_levels <- function(sps) {

  n_features <- length(unique(sps$feature_id))

  data.frame(
    msLevel = 2:4,
    n_spectra = as.integer(
      table(factor(Spectra::msLevel(sps), levels = 2:4))
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      mean_spectra = round(n_spectra / n_features, 2)
    )
}

# Before and after enrichment
before <- average_ms_levels(ftms_best)
after  <- average_ms_levels(ftms_final)

# Comparison
comparison_ms <- before |>
  rename(
    n_before = n_spectra,
    mean_before = mean_spectra
  ) |>
  left_join(
    after |>
      rename(
        n_after = n_spectra,
        mean_after = mean_spectra
      ),
    by = "msLevel"
  )

print(comparison_ms)
```

filter out all peaks that have intensity below 1% (or 0.5%) of the base peak

```{r}
filter_basepeak_intensity <- function(x, threshold = 0.01) {
  
  if (nrow(x) == 0)
    return(x)
  
  base_peak <- max(x[, 2], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  x[x[, 2] >= threshold * base_peak, , drop = FALSE]
}
```

```{r}
ftms_final <- addProcessing(
  ftms_final,
  function(x) {
    filter_basepeak_intensity(x, threshold = 0.01)
  }
)
```

Get max MS level per tree

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Convert to base data.frame
df <- as.data.frame(spectraData(ftms_final))

# Get max MS level per tree
final_levels <- tapply(df$msLevel, df$MergedMSntreeID, max, na.rm = TRUE)

# Count
table(final_levels)
```

## (Optional) evaluate based on known spectra

```{r}

idx <- which(round(ftms_final$precursorMz) == 1333)
idx
peaksData(ftms_final)[idx][[1]]

idx <- which(round(ftms_final$precursorMz) == 1171)
idx
peaksData(ftms_final)[idx][[1]]

```

This looks like a really good selection !

# Check MS levels in merged MSn trees

```{r}
# Extract spectraData from merged_spectra
merged_sd <- as.data.frame(spectraData(ftms_final))

# Count spectra per feature : MS level
feature_counts <- table(merged_sd$feature_id, merged_sd$msLevel)
feature_counts <- as.data.frame.matrix(feature_counts)  # columns = MS levels

# Define MS levels present
ms_levels <- colnames(feature_counts)

# Compute summary for each MS level with descriptive names
ms_summary <- lapply(ms_levels, function(ms) {
  counts <- feature_counts[[ms]]
  summary(counts)
})

# Set descriptive names
names(ms_summary) <- paste0("MS", ms_levels, " spectra per feature")

# Print summaries
ms_summary
```

# Save

Finally we verify if the number of unique features corresponds to the number of unique MergedMSntreeID to ensure that we have one tree per feature.

```{r}
length(unique(unlist(ftms_final$feature_id)))
length(unique(unlist(ftms_final$MergedMSntreeID)))
length(unique(unlist(ftms_final$MSntreeID)))
```

we have `r length(unique(merged_spectra$MergedMSntreeID))` unique feature and unique MSntreeID, That's mean that we have for each feature one representative tree.

Now we save the resulting ftms spectra object to a local directory.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
ftms_one_merged_tree <- ftms_final
save(
  ftms_one_merged_tree,
  file = here("data", "ftms_one_merged_tree.RData")
)
```

```{r}
ftms_assembled <- msntree_to_pseudoMS2(ftms_one_merged_tree)
ftms_assembled
unique(spectraData(ftms_assembled)$msLevel)

```

Add "individual" label to the initial object with separated spectrums

```{r}
spectraData(ftms_one_merged_tree)$spectrum.type <- "individual"
```

We concatenate the spectral tree and pseudo-MS² spectra generated above. First switch the storage backend of the Spectra objects to in-memory backend, which allows Efficient access to the spectral data since some backends may not support direct concatenation. Then combine them into a single Spectra object ftms_all The peaks and metadata of the concatenated spectra are then displayed for inspection.

```{r}
ftms_one_merged_tree <- setBackend(ftms_one_merged_tree,  MsBackendMemory())
ftms_assembled <- setBackend(ftms_assembled,  MsBackendMemory())

# Concatenate
ftms_all <- concatenateSpectra(ftms_one_merged_tree, ftms_assembled)

peaksData(ftms_all)[[1,]]            

head(spectraData(ftms_all), 3)
```

```{r}
save(
  ftms_all,
  file = here("data", "ftms_all.RData")
)

# Session information

sessionInfo()
```
